learning: If line_loss_events fall to 0 and max_error drops below 0.06 m, the next test is forward offset y = 0.06 m. If line losses persist at 1 per run, yaw inertia is not sufficient alone and the next test is mass 0.4 kg or a wheel_radius change, depending on progress.
notes: Mass-only test from the iteration 3 design: 0.7 to 0.5 kg, with the 16 mm footprint, 20 mm pitch, 0.10 m track and controller unchanged. Built to test whether reduced yaw inertia clears the persistent single line loss per run.
rationale: Iterations 0 to 3 all ended off_track in every trial. max_error sits at the 0.060 to 0.067 m off-track floor, line_loss_events is 1 per run on the last three designs, steering_oscillation is low (0.07 to 0.16), and progress is 0.10 to 0.18. Sensor pitch (10, 15, 20 mm), footprint (12 to 16 mm), track narrowing (0.12 to 0.10 m) and kp/kd (1.2/0.1 to 1.4/0.15) have each left max_error and line losses essentially unchanged. The untested lever is yaw inertia, so I deliver the Builder's iteration 4 geometry exactly: the iteration 3 design with mass reduced from 0.7 to 0.5 kg (about 29 percent less yaw inertia). The controller is held at the iteration 3 values (kp 1.4, ki 0.05, kd 0.15, base_speed 1.6, last_direction, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2]) so the mass result is attributable to the geometry alone. I make no claim about this run's outcome. Measurements include controller_errors and control_effort to catch any integration fault.
